title: Screenplay Template: Real Scripts From Short Films
summary: A free screenplay template to copy, with every element shown in the real script of SLOP, a short made in Flick, plus the full script as a PDF to download.
body_markdown:
### What is a screenplay template?


A screenplay template is a document already laid out in screenplay format, with a scene heading, action, character names, dialogue, parentheticals and transitions in their places. You replace the placeholder words with your own and the page keeps the format.


### What are the main elements of a screenplay?


A screenplay is built from six kinds of line: the scene heading (INT. or EXT., place and time), action in the present tense, the character name in capitals, dialogue, a parenthetical on how a line is said, and transitions such as CUT TO. Every scene starts with a heading.


### What font is a screenplay written in?


Screenplays are set in 12 point Courier, a typewriter face in which every letter takes the same width. That fixed width is what makes one page of a standard screenplay run about one minute on screen.


### How many pages is a short film screenplay?


A short film screenplay runs about one page per minute of screen time, so a short of 5 minutes is about 5 pages. SLOP, a short film made in Flick, turned 5 pages of script into a 2:32 film, so treat the rule as a rough guide rather than a timer.


### Do you need screenwriting software to use a screenplay template?


A screenplay template works in any text editor, because the format comes from capitals, blank lines and indents. Software such as Flick's Story view sets the indents for you and can read a plain text script saved as .fountain or .txt.


### Can you start a screenplay from a template in Flick?


Every new project in Flick opens its Story tab on a screenplay template: headings for the brief, narrative and creative direction, then the real script of the short film SLOP. You type over it, or ask the chat to write your script in its place.
